_readme: Registry seed for tracked state aircraft.
Rule from the brief: registration marks and ICAO 24-bit addresses are never guessed.
Every entry below carries the sources it rests on and a verificationStatus.
The CURRENT fleet of the MV SR air unit is OM-BYA, OM-BYK and OM-BYB. OM-BYC was
withdrawn on 2025-02-11 and is kept only as a historical record: status 'retired',
trackingEnabled false, activeUntil set. It must not appear in any figure describing
fleetKey attaches an aircraft to a cost model and a utilisation denominator. Aircraft
of another ministry belong to another fleetKey so that one ministry's operating rate
is never applied to another's aircraft.
verificationStatus = 'needs_verification' means: the identity is corroborated by the
listed sources, but not by a primary state register we can read ourselves. Slovak state
aircraft are deliberately absent from the civil register (Dopravny urad / NSAT), which we
checked - see notes. Upgrading these to 'verified' requires the military/state aircraft
register or a freedom-of-information answer from MV SR. See DATA_SOURCES.md.
Aircraft that look state-operated but turned out NOT to be are kept in 'rejected' below,
so nobody re-adds them from the same bad assumption.

sources.publisher: Dopravny urad / NSAT (Transport Authority of the Slovak Republic)
sources.title: Zoznam lietadiel zapisanych v registri lietadiel SR k 07.01.2026
sources.notes: Primary state source for CIVIL registrations. Used here as negative evidence: no A319 and no Fokker 100 appears in it, consistent with the government fleet being state aircraft outside the civil register.

sources.title: Letecky utvar Ministerstva vnutra Slovenskej republiky
sources.notes: Fleet composition and in-service dates. Tertiary source; corroborated by media reporting below.

sources.title: Ministerstvo vnutra vyraduje jedno z dvoch lietadiel Fokker 100, bude na nahradne diely
sources.notes: Withdrawal of OM-BYC from service on 2025-02-11.

sources.title: Community ADS-B aircraft database (ICAO 24-bit address to registration)
sources.notes: Source of the icao24 <-> registration mapping. Community-maintained, not an official register. This is the single weakest link in aircraft identity and the reason nothing here is marked 'verified'.

sources.title: Vianocna nadielka OS SR: Bizjety Bombardier Global 5000
sources.notes: Aviation trade press. Gives MSN 9513 (built 2013, 2 400 flight hours) and MSN 9633 (built 2014, 2 455 flight hours), acquired from United Wings International under contracts of 16 and 19 December 2024 worth USD 23.15 and 24.6 million.

aircraft.notes: Government flying service, operated by the Ministry of Interior air unit. In service since 2016-06-14. ICAO24 from tar1090-db; type and dates from sk/en Wikipedia. Not present in the NSAT civil register (checked 2026-08-21), as expected for a state aircraft.
Second A319 of the government flying service. Same caveats as OM-BYA.
Remaining airworthy Fokker 100 after OM-BYC was withdrawn in February 2025.

Withdrawn from service on 2025-02-11 and used as a source of spare parts for the remaining Fokker 100. Kept as a historical record only: it is excluded from the current fleet, from ADS-B polling, from cost allocation and utilisation, and from every dashboard figure describing the fleet today. Flights before the withdrawal date remain attributable to it if data for them is ever obtained.

Slovak military register, evidence number equals the MSN. Built 2013. Deliberately has no OM- mark: state aircraft in the military register are absent from the civil register, so absence there is not evidence against it. Acquisition contract signed December 2024; no sourced in-service date, so activeFrom is left unset. Previous marks are for provenance research only - flights under them predate Slovak ownership and carried different ICAO addresses.
Slovak military register, evidence number equals the MSN. Built 2014. Same caveats as 9513.

candidates.hypothesis: Former Ministry of Interior Mil Mi-17. The OM-BY* block is used by the ministry air unit, but this specific airframe is not confirmed.
Former Ministry of Interior Mil Mi-17. Slovak Mi-17 operations ended in September 2024 under sanctions on Russian spare parts; unconfirmed for this airframe.
AgustaWestland AW189 delivered to the ministry air unit in February 2025. No ICAO 24-bit address found in any source we can cite, so it is deliberately NOT seeded - we do not guess hex addresses.
Bell 429 police helicopter of the ministry air unit. ICAO 24-bit address unconfirmed.

rejected.reason: Look like state aircraft, are not. The NSAT civil register of 2026-01-07 lists them as owned by Slovak Training Academy, s.r.o. and operated by HELI COMPANY, s.r.o., with liens held by commercial entities. Private aircraft - out of scope for this project.

A privately operated Bombardier Global 5000: the NSAT civil register of 2026-01-07 gives the owner as Raiffeisen - Leasing, s.r.o. and the operator as ELITE JET s.r.o. Out of scope. NOTE: this entry once carried the conclusion that Slovakia therefore operates no state Global 5000. That was wrong, and wrong in the way this project exists to avoid - absence from one register is not absence in fact. The Slovak Air Force operates two, 9513 and 9633, in the military register. They are seeded above.

operators.name: Statna letecka preprava Slovenskej republiky
operators.notes: Umbrella only. It is not an operator itself; the two ministries below are, and they have separate budgets, separate registers and separate operating costs.

operators.name: Letecky utvar Ministerstva vnutra Slovenskej republiky
operators.notes: The government flying service. Civil OM- registrations, absent from the civil register because they are state aircraft.

operators.name: Vzdusne sily Ozbrojenych sil Slovenskej republiky
operators.notes: Ministry of Defence. Aircraft carry military evidence numbers in the military aircraft register, not OM- marks.
